title.zh: 卷一百十五 列傳第四十五: 二國外記
title.en: Volume 115 Biographies 45: Two Records of Foreign Countries
title.raw: 卷一百十五 列傳第四十五: 二國外記 Volume 115 Biographies 45: Two Records of Foreign Countries

sentences.zh: 高麗自有國以來，傳次久近，人民土田，歷代各有其志，然高麗與遼，相為終始二百餘年。

translations.literal: Since Goryeo has had its own state, the length of succession, its people and lands—each generation has pursued its own aims; yet Goryeo and Liao were bound to each other from first to last for more than two hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Goryeo became a kingdom, its royal succession, population, and territory each generation followed its own course; nevertheless Goryeo and the Liao were locked in relations that ran their full course for over two hundred years.

sentences.zh: 自太祖皇帝神冊間，高麗遣使進寶劍。

translations.literal: From the Shence era of Emperor Taizu, Goryeo sent envoys to present a precious sword.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shence reign of the Taizu Emperor, Goryeo dispatched envoys bearing a treasured sword as tribute.

sentences.zh: 天贊三年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianzan, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianzan, they presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 太宗天顯二年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianxian under Emperor Taizong, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianxian of Emperor Taizong, they came to offer tribute.

sentences.zh: 會同二年，受晉上尊號冊，遣使往報。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huitong, when he received the honorific title register from Jin, he sent envoys to report this.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huitong, after receiving the honorific-title document from Jin, the court sent envoys to notify Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 聖宗統和三年秋七月，詔諸道各完戎器，以備東征高麗。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn in the third year of Tonghe under Emperor Shenzong, an edict ordered each circuit to complete its weapons in preparation for an eastern campaign against Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn in the third year of Tonghe, Emperor Shenzong ordered every circuit to ready its arms for an eastern expedition against Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 八月，以遼澤沮洳，罷師。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, because the Liao marshes were waterlogged, the army was withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the campaign was called off, the Liao marshes being too boggy.

sentences.zh: 十年，以東京留守蕭恒德伐高麗。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Xiao Hengde, Military Governor of the Eastern Capital, was sent to attack Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, Xiao Hengde as Military Governor of the Eastern Capital led a campaign against Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 十一年，王治遣樸良柔奉表請罪，詔取女直國鴨淥江東數百里地賜之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Wang Zhi sent Pak Yang-nyeo with a memorial begging forgiveness; an edict took several hundred li of land east of the Yalu River in the Jurchen country and granted it to them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, King Wang Zhi sent Pak Yang-nyeo with a memorial pleading for pardon; the court decreed that several hundred li of territory east of the Yalu in Jurchen lands be ceded to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 十二年，入貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year they presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 三月，王治遣使請所俘生口，詔贖還之，仍遣使撫諭。

translations.literal: In the third month, Wang Zhi sent envoys requesting the captives who had been taken; an edict ordered them ransomed and returned, and envoys were still sent to console and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Wang Zhi asked for the return of captives; the court ordered them redeemed and sent envoys to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，王治進妓樂，詔卻之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Wang Zhi presented singing girls and musicians; an edict refused them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Wang Zhi offered female entertainers and musicians; the court declined them.

sentences.zh: 十三年，治遣李周楨來貢，又進鷹。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Zhi sent Li Zhouzhen to pay tribute, and also presented hawks.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, Zhi sent Li Zhouzhen with tribute and also presented hunting hawks.

sentences.zh: 十月，遣李知白奉貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Li Zhibai was sent to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Li Zhibai was dispatched with tribute.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遣使冊治為王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, envoys were sent to invest Zhi as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, envoys were sent to invest Wang Zhi as king of Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 遣童子十人來學本國語。

translations.literal: Ten boys were sent to study the language of our state.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo sent ten youths to learn the Khitan language.

sentences.zh: 十四年，王治表乞為婚姻，以東京留守駙馬蕭恒德女下嫁之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, King Wang Zhi memorialized requesting a marriage alliance; the daughter of Xiao Hengde, Military Governor of the Eastern Capital and imperial son-in-law, was given to him in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, Wang Zhi petitioned for a marital alliance; the court married him to the daughter of Xiao Hengde, Military Governor of the Eastern Capital and imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 六月，遣使來問起居。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, envoys were sent to inquire after the emperor's health.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, envoys came to inquire after the emperor's well-being.

sentences.zh: 自是至者無時。

translations.literal: From this time onward, they came without fixed season.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, tribute missions arrived at irregular intervals.

sentences.zh: 五月，高麗西京留守康肇弒其主誦，擅立誦從兄詢。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Kang Zhao, Military Governor of Goryeo's Western Capital, murdered his lord Song and on his own authority installed Song's cousin Xun.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Kang Zhao, Western Capital Military Governor of Goryeo, assassinated King Song and installed Song's cousin Xun without authorization.

sentences.zh: 八月，聖宗自將伐高麗，報宋，遣引進使韓杞宣問詢。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Emperor Shenzong personally led a campaign against Goryeo, notified Song, and sent the Introducing Commissioner Han Qi to announce and question Xun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Shenzong led the campaign in person, informed the Song court, and sent Introducing Commissioner Han Qi to proclaim the charges against Xun.

sentences.zh: 詢奉表乞罷師，不許。

translations.literal: Xun submitted a memorial begging that the army be withdrawn; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xun sent a memorial pleading for withdrawal of the army; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 十一月，大軍渡鴨淥江，康肇拒戰於銅州，敗之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the great army crossed the Yalu River; Kang Zhao resisted at Tong Prefecture and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the main force crossed the Yalu; Kang Zhao gave battle at Tong Prefecture and was routed.

sentences.zh: 肇復出，右皮室詳穩耶律敵魯擒肇等，追奔數十里，獲所棄糧餉、鎧仗，銅、霍、貴、寧等州皆降。

translations.literal: Zhao came out again; Yelü Dilu, detailed commander of the Right Pishi Army, captured Zhao and others, pursued the fleeing enemy for several tens of li, and seized abandoned grain, armor, and weapons; Tong, Huo, Gui, Ning, and other prefectures all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao sallied forth again; Yelü Dilu of the Right Pishi Army captured Zhao and his party, pursued them for dozens of li, and recovered abandoned provisions and arms; Tong, Huo, Gui, Ning, and other prefectures submitted.

sentences.zh: 詢上表請朝，許之，禁軍士俘掠。

translations.literal: Xun submitted a memorial requesting an audience; this was granted, and the troops were forbidden to seize captives for plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Xun petitioned to come to court; permission was granted and the soldiers were forbidden to take captives by force.

sentences.zh: 以政事舍人馬保祐為開京留守，安州團練使王八為副留守。

translations.literal: Ma Baoyou, Administrative Associate, was made Military Governor of Kaesong; Wang Ba, Militia Training Commissioner of An Prefecture, was made deputy military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Baoyou, Administrative Associate, was appointed Military Governor of Kaesong, with Wang Ba, Militia Training Commissioner of An Prefecture, as deputy.

sentences.zh: 太子太師乙凜將騎兵一千，送保祐等赴京。

translations.literal: Yiling, Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, led one thousand cavalry to escort Baoyou and the others to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent Yiling led a thousand horsemen to escort Baoyou and his party to the capital.

sentences.zh: 守將卓思正殺我使者韓喜孫等十人，領兵出拒，保祐等復還。

translations.literal: The defending commander Zhuo Sizheng killed our envoys Han Xisun and nine others, led troops out to resist, and Baoyou and the others returned.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander Zhuo Sizheng killed ten of our envoys including Han Xisun, marched out to resist, and Baoyou and his party fell back.

sentences.zh: 乙凜領兵擊之，思正遂奔西京。

translations.literal: Yiling led troops to attack him; Sizheng then fled to the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yiling attacked him; Sizheng fled to the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 圍之五日，不克，駐蹕於城西佛寺。

translations.literal: They besieged it for five days without taking it, and the emperor halted at a Buddhist temple west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: After a five-day siege failed, the emperor encamped at a Buddhist temple west of the city.

sentences.zh: 高麗禮部郎中渤海陀失來降。

translations.literal: Tuoshi, a Bureau of Rites official of Bohai origin in Goryeo, came over to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoshi, a Goryeo Bureau of Rites official of Bohai descent, defected.

sentences.zh: 遣排押、盆奴攻開京，遇敵於京西，敗之。

translations.literal: Paiya and Pannu were sent to attack Kaesong; they met the enemy west of the capital and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Paiya and Pannu attacked Kaesong, met the enemy west of the city, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 詢棄城遁走，遂焚開京，至清江而還。

translations.literal: Xun abandoned the city and fled; they then burned Kaesong and returned as far as the Qing River.
translations.idiomatic: Xun abandoned Kaesong and fled; the army burned the city and withdrew to the Qing River.

sentences.zh: 二十九年正月，班師，所降諸城復叛。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-ninth year, the army withdrew; the cities that had surrendered rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-ninth year the army withdrew, and the surrendered cities rose again.

sentences.zh: 至貴州南嶺谷，大雨連日，霽乃得渡，馬駝皆疲乏，甲仗多遺棄。

translations.literal: At the Southern Ridge Valley of Gui Prefecture, heavy rain fell for many days; only when it cleared could they cross; horses and camels were all exhausted, and much armor and equipment was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: At the Southern Ridge Valley south of Gui Prefecture, rain fell for days; they crossed only after it cleared, with horses and camels spent and much armor cast away.

sentences.zh: 次鴨淥江，以所俘人分置諸陵廟，余賜內戚、大臣。

translations.literal: When they reached the Yalu River, the captives were distributed among the imperial tombs and temples; the remainder were given to imperial affines and great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yalu, captives were assigned to the imperial mausoleums and temples; the rest were granted to imperial kin and senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 開泰元年，詢遣蔡忠順來乞稱臣如舊，詔詢親朝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaitai, Xun sent Cai Zhongshun to beg to submit as a subject as before; an edict ordered Xun to come to court in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaitai, Xun sent Cai Zhongshun to plead for restoration of vassal status; the court commanded Xun to attend in person.

sentences.zh: 八月，遣田拱之奉表，稱病不能朝。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Tian Gongzhi was sent with a memorial, claiming illness and inability to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Tian Gongzhi presented a memorial on Xun's behalf, citing illness that prevented him from coming to court.

sentences.zh: 詔復取六州之地。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the recovery of the territory of the six prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued to retake the six prefectures.

sentences.zh: 二年，耶律資忠使高麗取地，未幾還。

translations.literal: In the second year, Yelü Zizhong was sent to Goryeo to take territory; before long he returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Yelü Zizhong was sent to Goryeo to seize territory and soon returned.

sentences.zh: 三年，資忠復使，如前索地。

translations.literal: In the third year, Zizhong was sent again to demand territory as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Zizhong was dispatched again with the same demand for territory.

sentences.zh: 五月，詔國舅詳穩蕭敵烈、東京留守耶律團石等造浮梁於鴨淥江，城保、宣義、定遠等州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, an edict ordered the State Uncle and detailed commander Xiao Dilie, Military Governor of the Eastern Capital Yelü Tuanshi, and others to build a pontoon bridge on the Yalu and fortify Bao, Xuanyi, Dingyuan, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, the court ordered State Uncle Xiao Dilie, Eastern Capital Military Governor Yelü Tuanshi, and others to erect a pontoon bridge on the Yalu and garrison Bao, Xuanyi, Dingyuan, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 四年，命北府宰相劉慎行為都統，樞密使耶律世良為副，殿前都點檢蕭虛烈為都監。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Liu Shenxing of the Northern Chancellery was appointed supreme commander, Yelü Shiliang, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, as deputy, and Xiao Xulie, Chief Palace Inspector, as chief overseer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Northern Chancellery Chancellor Liu Shenxing was named supreme commander, Bureau of Military Affairs Commissioner Yelü Shiliang as deputy, and Chief Palace Inspector Xiao Xulie as chief overseer.

sentences.zh: 慎行挈家邊上，致緩師期，追還之，以世良、虛烈總兵伐高麗。

translations.literal: Shenxing brought his family to the frontier and thereby delayed the campaign schedule; he was recalled, and Shiliang and Xulie took overall command to attack Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing moved his household to the border and missed the campaign deadline; recalled, he was replaced by Shiliang and Xulie, who led the army against Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 五年，世良等與高麗戰於郭州西，破之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Shiliang and the others fought Goryeo west of Guo Prefecture and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Shiliang and his forces defeated the Goryeo army west of Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六年，樞密使蕭合卓為都統，漢人行宮都部署王繼忠為副，殿前都點檢蕭虛烈為都監進討。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Xiao Hezhuo, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made supreme commander; Wang Jizhong, Chief Deployer of the Han Palace Mobile Camp, was deputy; Xiao Xulie, Chief Palace Inspector, was chief overseer for the advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Military Affairs Commissioner Xiao Hezhuo became supreme commander, Han Mobile Camp Chief Deployer Wang Jizhong deputy, and Chief Palace Inspector Xiao Xulie chief overseer of the advance.

sentences.zh: 蕭合卓攻興化軍不克，師還。

translations.literal: Xiao Hezhuo attacked Xinghua Army without success and the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Hezhuo besieged Xinghua Army unsuccessfully and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔東平郡王蕭排押為都統，蕭虛烈為副統，東京留守耶律八哥為都監，復伐高麗。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict made Eastern Peace Prince Xiao Paiya supreme commander, Xiao Xulie deputy commander, and Eastern Capital Military Governor Yelü Bage chief overseer, to attack Goryeo again.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Eastern Peace Prince Xiao Paiya was appointed supreme commander, Xiao Xulie deputy, and Eastern Capital Military Governor Yelü Bage chief overseer for another Goryeo campaign.

sentences.zh: 十二月，蕭排押與戰於茶、陀二河之間，我軍不利，天雲、右皮室二軍沒溺者眾，天雲軍詳穩海裏、遙輦帳詳穩阿果達、客省使酌古、渤海詳穩高清明等皆沒於陣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Xiao Paiya fought between the Cha and Tuo rivers; our army was unfavorable, and many of the Tianyun and Right Pishi armies were drowned; Hai Li, detailed commander of the Tianyun Army, Aguoda, detailed commander of the Yaolian Account Army, Guest Reception Commissioner Zhuogu, Bohai detailed commander Gao Qingming, and others all perished in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Xiao Paiya fought between the Cha and Tuo rivers; our forces fared badly, and many men of the Tianyun and Right Pishi armies drowned; detailed commanders Hai Li and Aguoda, Guest Reception Commissioner Zhuogu, Bohai detailed commander Gao Qingming, and others fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔數排押討高麗罪，釋之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict several times charged Paiya with the crime of campaigning against Goryeo, then pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, the court repeatedly arraigned Paiya for failures in the Goryeo war, then pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 加有功將校，益封戰沒將校之妻，錄其子弟。

translations.literal: Meritorious officers were promoted in rank; the wives of officers who died in battle received additional enfeoffments, and their sons and younger brothers were enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: Officers who had distinguished themselves were promoted; widows of the fallen received added fiefs, and their sons and younger brothers were entered on the rolls.

sentences.zh: 以南皮室軍校有功，賜衣物銀絹有差，出金帛賜肴裏、涅哥二奚軍。

translations.literal: Because officers of the Southern Pishi Army had merit, clothing, silver, and silk were bestowed in differing amounts; gold and silk were issued to reward the Xiao and Niege Jurchen armies.
translations.idiomatic: Officers of the Southern Pishi Army were rewarded with clothing, silver, and silk according to merit; gold and silk were granted to the Xiao and Niege Jurchen forces.

sentences.zh: 八月，遣郎君曷不呂等率諸部兵，會大軍同討高麗。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Langjun Yebu and others led the troops of the various tribes to join the main army in a joint campaign against Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Langjun Yebu and others led tribal levies to unite with the main force against Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 詢遣使來乞貢方物。

translations.literal: Xun sent envoys to beg to present local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Xun sent envoys asking permission to resume tribute offerings.

sentences.zh: 九年，資忠還，以詢降表進，釋詢罪。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Zizhong returned and presented Xun's surrender memorial; Xun's crimes were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, Zizhong returned with Xun's submission memorial, and Xun was absolved.

sentences.zh: 太平元年，詢薨，遣使來報嗣位，即遣使冊王欽為王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiping, Xun died; envoys came to report the succession, and envoys were immediately sent to invest Wang Qin as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiping, Xun died; Goryeo reported the succession, and the court at once invested Wang Qin as king.

sentences.zh: 九年，賜欽物。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, gifts were bestowed on Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, presents were granted to Qin.

sentences.zh: 十一年，聖宗崩，遣使告哀。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Emperor Shenzong died; envoys came to announce the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, upon Shenzong's death, Goryeo sent envoys to announce the bereavement.

sentences.zh: 七月，使來慰奠。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, envoys came to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, envoys arrived to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 興宗重熙七年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chongxi under Emperor Xingzong, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Chongxi of Emperor Xingzong, they presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 十二年三月，以加上尊號，來賀。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twelfth year, when the honorific title was added, they came to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twelfth year, they came to congratulate the bestowal of an honorific title.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, envoys came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, tribute envoys arrived.

sentences.zh: 十四年三月，又來貢。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourteenth year, they again came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourteenth year, they presented tribute again.

sentences.zh: 十五年，入貢。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year they offered tribute.

sentences.zh: 八月，王欽薨，遣使來告。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, King Wang Qin died; envoys came to announce it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Wang Qin died; envoys reported his death.

sentences.zh: 十六年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year they presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 明年，又來貢。

translations.literal: The next year, they again came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they came with tribute again.

sentences.zh: 十九年，復貢。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, they presented tribute again.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year they offered tribute once more.

sentences.zh: 六月，遣使來賀伐夏之捷。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, envoys were sent to congratulate the victory over Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, envoys came to congratulate the defeat of Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，入貢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year they presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 二十三年四月，王徽請官其子，詔加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-third year, Wang Hui requested an office for his son; an edict added the title of Honorary Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twenty-third year, Wang Hui asked that his son be given an office; the court granted him Honorary Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 興宗崩，道宗即位，清寧元年八月，遣使報國哀，以先帝遺留物賜之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xingzong died and Emperor Daozong succeeded, in the eighth month of the first year of Qingning envoys were sent to announce the national mourning, and objects left by the late emperor were bestowed on them.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingzong's death and Daozong's accession, in the eighth month of the first year of Qingning, Goryeo was notified of the national mourning and given gifts from the late emperor's estate.

sentences.zh: 十一月，使來會葬。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, envoys came to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, envoys came to take part in the funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 二年、三年，皆來貢。

translations.literal: In the second and third years, they all came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second and third years they presented tribute each year.

sentences.zh: 四年春，遣使報太皇太后哀。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, envoys were sent to announce the mourning of the Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year, envoys announced the Grand Empress Dowager's death.

sentences.zh: 五月，使來會葬。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, envoys came to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, envoys came for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 咸雍七年、八年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the seventh and eighth years of Xianyong, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh and eighth years of Xianyong they presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以佛經一藏賜徽。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, one set of Buddhist scriptures was bestowed on Hui.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, a complete Buddhist canon was granted to Wang Hui.

sentences.zh: 九年、十年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth and tenth years, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth and tenth years they offered tribute.

sentences.zh: 大康二年三月，皇太后崩，遣使報哀。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Dakang, the Empress Dowager died; envoys were sent to announce the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Dakang, upon the Empress Dowager's death, envoys announced the mourning.

sentences.zh: 六月，使來吊祭。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, envoys came to offer libations and sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, envoys came to perform mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 四年，王徽乞賜鴨淥江以東地，不許。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Wang Hui begged that land east of the Yalu River be granted; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Wang Hui petitioned for territory east of the Yalu; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 九年八月，王徽薨，以徽子三韓國公勛權知國事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the ninth year, Wang Hui died; Hui's son, the Duke of the Three Han States Xun, was ordered to manage state affairs provisionally.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the ninth year, Wang Hui died; his son Xun, Duke of the Three Han States, was authorized to govern provisionally.

sentences.zh: 十二月，勛薨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Xun died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Xun died.

sentences.zh: 大安元年，冊勛子運為國王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Da'an, Xun's son Yun was invested as king of the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Da'an, Xun's son Yun was invested as king.

sentences.zh: 二年，遣使來謝封冊。

translations.literal: In the second year, envoys came to thank the court for the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, envoys came to express gratitude for the investiture.

sentences.zh: 三年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the third year, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year they presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，免歲貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year, the annual tribute was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year, annual tribute was waived.

sentences.zh: 五年、六年，連貢。

translations.literal: In the fifth and sixth years, they presented tribute in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth and sixth years they offered tribute in consecutive years.

sentences.zh: 九年，賜王運羊。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, sheep were bestowed on King Yun.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, the court granted sheep to King Yun.

sentences.zh: 十年，運薨，子昱遣使來告，即賻贈。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Yun died; his son Yu sent envoys to announce it, and funeral gifts were immediately bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, Yun died; his son Yu reported the death, and funeral gifts were sent at once.

sentences.zh: 壽隆元年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shoulong, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shoulong they presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 十一月，王昱病，命其子颙權知國事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, King Yu fell ill and ordered his son Yong to manage state affairs provisionally.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Yu fell ill and appointed his son Yong to govern provisionally.

sentences.zh: 二年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the second year, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year they offered tribute.

sentences.zh: 三年三月，王昱薨。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year, King Yu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year, Wang Yu died.

sentences.zh: 五年，王颙乞封冊。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Wang Yong begged for investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Wang Yong petitioned for formal investiture.

sentences.zh: 六年，封颙為三韓國公。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Yong was enfeoffed as Duke of the Three Han States.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Yong was enfeoffed as Duke of the Three Han States.

sentences.zh: 七年，道宗崩，天祚即位，改為乾統元年，報道宗哀，使來慰奠。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Emperor Daozong died and Tianzuo succeeded; the reign was changed to the first year of Qiantong, the mourning for Daozong was announced, and envoys came to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, after Daozong's death and Tianzuo's accession, the era became Qiantong year one; Goryeo was notified of the mourning and sent envoys to console the court.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遣使來賀。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, envoys came to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, envoys came with congratulations.

sentences.zh: 五年，三韓國公颙薨，子俁遣使來告。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Duke of the Three Han States Yong died; his son Yu sent envoys to announce it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Duke Yong died; his son Yu sent envoys to report the death.

sentences.zh: 八年，封俁為三韓國公，贈其父颙為國王。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Yu was enfeoffed as Duke of the Three Han States, and his father Yong was posthumously granted the title of king.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, Yu was enfeoffed Duke of the Three Han States and his father Yong was posthumously made king.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遣使來謝。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, envoys came to express thanks.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, envoys came to offer thanks.

sentences.zh: 九年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year they presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 天慶二年，王俁母薨，來告，遣使致祭，起復。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqing, the mother of King Yu died; they came to announce it; envoys were sent to perform sacrifices, and he was ordered to resume office after mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqing, upon the death of Wang Yu's mother, Goryeo reported the bereavement; the court sent envoys to sacrifice and ordered Yu's return to duty after mourning.

sentences.zh: 三年，遣使來謝致祭，又來謝起復。

translations.literal: In the third year, envoys came to thank the court for performing sacrifices, and again came to thank for the order to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, envoys thanked the court for the sacrificial rites and again thanked for permission to leave mourning.

sentences.zh: 十年，乞兵於高麗以禦金，而金人責之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, they begged troops from Goryeo to resist Jin, and the Jin people held them accountable.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, Liao asked Goryeo for troops against the Jin; the Jin held Goryeo responsible.

sentences.zh: 至是遼國亡矣。

translations.literal: At this point the Liao state perished.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Liao dynasty had fallen.

sentences.zh: ○西夏

translations.literal: ○ Western Xia
translations.idiomatic: ○ Western Xia

sentences.zh: 西夏，本魏拓跋氏後，其地則赫連國也。

translations.literal: Western Xia was originally descended from the Tuoba clan of Wei; its territory had been the state of Helian.
translations.idiomatic: Western Xia traced its line to the Tuoba of Northern Wei; its lands had once formed the Helian kingdom.

sentences.zh: 遠祖思恭，唐季受賜姓曰李，涉五代至宋，世有其地。

translations.literal: The remote ancestor Sigong, in the late Tang, received the bestowed surname Li; through the Five Dynasties down to Song, the family held its lands in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Their distant forebear Sigong received the surname Li in late Tang times; through the Five Dynasties into Song, the clan kept its domain generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 至李繼遷始大，據夏、銀、綏、宥、靜五州，緣境七鎮，其東西二十五驛，南北十餘驛。

translations.literal: When Li Jiqian first grew powerful, he held the five prefectures of Xia, Yin, Sui, You, and Jing, seven border garrisons along the frontier, twenty-five courier stations east and west, and more than ten stations north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Under Li Jiqian the realm first expanded, holding Xia, Yin, Sui, You, and Jing prefectures, seven frontier commands, twenty-five relay posts east and west, and more than ten north and south.

sentences.zh: 子德明，曉佛書，通法律，嘗觀《太一金鑒訣》、《野戰歌》，制番書十二卷，又制字若符篆。

translations.literal: His son Deming understood Buddhist texts and was versed in law; he once studied the "Taiyi Golden Mirror Formula" and "Song of Field Battle," compiled twelve volumes of Tangut script, and also devised characters resembling seal script.
translations.idiomatic: His son Deming knew Buddhist writings and legal codes, studied the 《Taiyi Golden Mirror Formula》 and 《Song of Field Battle》, compiled twelve volumes in the Tangut script, and devised characters resembling seal script.

sentences.zh: 其俗，衣白窄衫，氈冠，冠後垂紅結綬。

translations.literal: Their custom: they wore narrow white shirts, felt caps, and behind the cap hung a red knotted sash.
translations.idiomatic: In dress they wore narrow white shirts and felt caps with a red knotted cord hanging behind.

sentences.zh: 自號嵬名，設官分文武。

translations.literal: They styled themselves Weiming and established offices dividing civil and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They took the style Weiming and organized government into civil and military ranks.

sentences.zh: 其冠用金縷貼，間起雲，銀紙帖，緋衣，金塗銀帶，佩蹀躞、解錐、短刀、弓矢，穿靴，禿發，耳重環，紫旋襕六襲。

translations.literal: Their crowns used gold filigree with cloud motifs between, silver paper appliqué, scarlet robes, gold-plated silver belts; they wore gaiters, knife-sheath pendants, short knives, bow and arrows, boots, shaved their heads, wore heavy ear-rings, and six layers of purple twisted-lapel robes.
translations.idiomatic: Official crowns bore gold filigree clouds and silver appliqué; scarlet robes and gold-plated silver belts; accoutrements included gaiters, knife pendants, short blades, bows and arrows, boots, shaved heads, heavy ear-rings, and six layers of purple twisted-lapel garments.

sentences.zh: 出入乘馬，張青蓋，以二旗前引，從者百餘騎。

translations.literal: Going out and coming in they rode horses, spread a blue canopy, had two banners lead before them, and were followed by more than a hundred horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: They traveled on horseback beneath a blue canopy, preceded by two banners and escorted by more than a hundred riders.

sentences.zh: 民庶衣青綠。

translations.literal: The common people wore blue and green.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners dressed in blue and green.

sentences.zh: 革樂之五音為一音，裁禮之九拜為三拜。

translations.literal: They reduced the five tones of leather music to one tone, and trimmed the nine bows of ritual to three bows.
translations.idiomatic: They compressed the five tones of hide drums into a single tone and reduced the nine ritual prostrations to three.

sentences.zh: 凡出兵先卜，有四：一炙勃焦，以艾灼羊胛骨；

translations.literal: Whenever they took the field they divined first; there were four methods: first, roasting the scapula—burning moxa on the sheep shoulder blade;
translations.idiomatic: Before campaigning they always divined by four methods: first, scapulimancy—burning moxa on a sheep shoulder blade;

sentences.zh: 二擗算，擗竹於地以求數，若揲蓍然；

translations.literal: second, splitting tallies—splitting bamboo on the ground to obtain numbers, as in casting yarrow stalks;
translations.idiomatic: second, tally-casting—splitting bamboo on the ground for numbers, as with yarrow stalks;

sentences.zh: 三咒羊，其夜牽羊，焚香禱之，又焚谷火於野，次晨屠羊，腸胃通則吉，羊心有血則敗；

translations.literal: third, cursing the sheep—at night they led out a sheep, burned incense and prayed to it, and also burned grain fire in the wild; the next morning they butchered the sheep; if the entrails were clear it was auspicious, if blood appeared in the sheep's heart it was ill-omened;
translations.idiomatic: third, the sheep curse—at night a sheep was led out, incense burned and prayers offered, and grain fires lit in the open; at dawn the sheep was slaughtered; clear entrails meant good fortune, blood in the heart meant defeat;

sentences.zh: 四矢擊弦，聽其聲，知勝負及敵至之期。

translations.literal: fourth, striking the bowstring with an arrow and listening to the sound to know victory or defeat and the time of the enemy's arrival.
translations.idiomatic: fourth, shooting an arrow at the bowstring and reading victory, defeat, and the enemy's approach from the sound.

sentences.zh: 病者不用醫藥，召巫者送鬼，西夏語以巫為「廝」也；

translations.literal: The sick did not use medicine or physicians; they summoned shamans to send off ghosts—in Xia language the shaman was called "si";
translations.idiomatic: The ill relied not on medicine but on shamans to drive off spirits—the Xia word for shaman was "si";

sentences.zh: 或遷他室，謂之「閃病」。

translations.literal: or they moved to another dwelling, which was called "flashing the illness."
translations.idiomatic: or they moved to another house, called "flashing the illness."

sentences.zh: 喜報仇，有喪則不伐人，負甲葉於背識之。

translations.literal: They delighted in avenging wrongs; when in mourning they did not attack others, and they marked themselves by wearing leaves of armor on the back.
translations.idiomatic: They prized blood vengeance; while in mourning they refrained from raiding and marked themselves by wearing armor-leaves on the back.

sentences.zh: 仇解，用雞豬犬血和酒，貯於髑髏中飲之，乃誓曰：「若復報仇，穀麥不收，男女禿癩，六畜死，蛇入帳。

translations.literal: When enmity was settled, they mixed chicken, pig, and dog blood with wine, stored it in a skull and drank it, then swore: "If vengeance is taken again, grain and millet will not be harvested, men and women will go bald and leprous, the six livestock will die, and snakes will enter the tent.
translations.idiomatic: To end a feud they mixed chicken, pig, and dog blood with wine, drank from a skull, and swore: "Should vengeance be renewed, grain will fail, men and women go bald and leprous, livestock perish, and snakes enter the tent."

sentences.zh: 」有力小不能復仇者，集壯婦，享以牛羊酒食，趨讎家縱火，焚其廬舍。

translations.literal: Those too weak to take revenge gathered strong women, feasted them with oxen, sheep, wine, and food, and rushed to the enemy's house to set fire and burn down the dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: If too weak to revenge, they assembled strong women, feasted them with cattle, sheep, and wine, and rushed the foe's home to burn it down.

sentences.zh: 俗曰敵女兵不祥，輒避去。

translations.literal: Their custom held that enemy women-soldiers were inauspicious, and they always avoided them.
translations.idiomatic: They held enemy women warriors ill-omened and always avoided them.

sentences.zh: 訴於官，官擇舌辯氣直之人為和斷，官聽其屈直。

translations.literal: When they brought suit to the officials, the officials chose men eloquent of tongue and upright in spirit to mediate and decide, and the officials heard their right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Litigants appealed to officials, who chose eloquent, upright men to arbitrate and judged the merits of each side.

sentences.zh: 殺人者，納命價錢百二十千。

translations.literal: For murder, a life-price of one hundred and twenty thousand cash was paid.
translations.idiomatic: Murder was settled by a life-price of one hundred and twenty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 土產大麥、蓽豆、青稞、皞子、古子蔓、堿地蓬實、蓯蓉苗、小蕪荑、席雞草子、地黃葉、登廂草、沙蔥、野韭、拒灰、白蒿、堿地松實。

translations.literal: Local products included barley, pi beans, highland barley, haozi, guzi vines, alkali-field thistle fruit, cistanche sprouts, small fennel, mat-rush seeds, rehmannia leaves, dengxiang grass, wild scallion, wild leek, juhui, white artemisia, and alkali-field pine nuts.
translations.idiomatic: Local produce included barley, pi beans, highland barley, haozi, guzi vines, alkali thistle, cistanche sprouts, small fennel, mat-rush seed, rehmannia leaves, dengxiang grass, wild scallion, wild leek, juhui, white artemisia, and alkali pine nuts.

sentences.zh: 民年十五為丁。

translations.literal: At age fifteen a man became a ding.
translations.idiomatic: Men were counted as ding at age fifteen.

sentences.zh: 有二丁者，取一為正軍。

translations.literal: Where there were two ding, one was taken as a regular soldier.
translations.idiomatic: Households with two ding furnished one regular soldier.

sentences.zh: 負擔雜使一人為抄，四丁為兩抄。

translations.literal: One man served as porter and miscellaneous attendant for each soldier; four ding furnished two such attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Each regular soldier had one porter-attendant; four ding supplied two attendants.

sentences.zh: 餘人得射它丁，皆習戰鬥。

translations.literal: The remainder could shoot at other ding; all were trained for battle.
translations.idiomatic: The rest could be drafted from other ding; all were trained for war.

sentences.zh: 正軍馬駝各一，每家自置一帳。

translations.literal: Each regular soldier had one horse and one camel; each household set up one tent.
translations.idiomatic: Regular soldiers each had a horse and camel; every household kept one tent.

sentences.zh: 團練使上，帳、弓、矢各一，馬五百匹，橐駝一，旗鼓五，槍、劍、棍棓、少袋、雨氈、渾脫、鍬、钁、箭牌、鐵笊籬各一；

translations.literal: For Militia Training Commissioners and above: one tent, bow, and arrows each; five hundred horses, one camel, five drums and banners, and one each of spear, sword, club, small bag, rain felt, felt coat, shovel, hoe, arrow shield, and iron rake;
translations.idiomatic: Militia Training Commissioners and above received one tent, bow, and quiver each, five hundred horses, one camel, five drums and banners, and one each of spear, sword, club, small bag, rain felt, felt coat, shovel, hoe, arrow shield, and iron rake;

sentences.zh: 刺史以下，人各一駝，箭三百，毛幕一；

translations.literal: for Prefects and below, each man one camel, three hundred arrows, one felt tent;
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and below: one camel, three hundred arrows, and one felt tent per man;

sentences.zh: 餘兵三人共一幕。

translations.literal: the remaining soldiers shared one tent among three men.
translations.idiomatic: other troops shared one tent among three.

sentences.zh: 有炮手二百人，號「潑喜」。

translations.literal: There were two hundred artillerymen called "Poxi."
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred artillerymen were called "Poxi."

sentences.zh: 勇健者號「撞令郎」。

translations.literal: The valiant were called "Zhuanglinglang."
translations.idiomatic: Brave fighters were styled "Zhuanglinglang."

sentences.zh: 賫糧不過一旬。

translations.literal: Provisions carried did not exceed ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Marching rations did not exceed ten days.

sentences.zh: 晝則舉煙、揚塵，夜則篝火為候。

translations.literal: By day they raised smoke and dust; by night they lit beacon fires as signals.
translations.idiomatic: By day they signaled with smoke and dust; by night with beacon fires.

sentences.zh: 若獲人馬，射之，號曰殺鬼招魂。

translations.literal: If they captured men or horses, they shot them, calling it "shooting ghosts to summon souls."
translations.idiomatic: Captives of men or horses were shot in a rite called "shooting ghosts to summon souls."

sentences.zh: 或射草縛人。

translations.literal: Or they shot straw figures bound as men.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes they shot straw effigies bound like men.

sentences.zh: 出軍用單日，避晦日。

translations.literal: They marched on odd-numbered days and avoided even-numbered days.
translations.idiomatic: Armies marched on odd days and avoided even days.

sentences.zh: 多立虛寨，設伏兵。

translations.literal: They set up many empty camps and laid ambushes.
translations.idiomatic: They erected many decoy camps and laid ambushes.

sentences.zh: 衣重甲，乘善馬，以鐵騎為前鋒，用鉤索絞聯，雖死馬上不落。

translations.literal: They wore heavy armor, rode good horses, used iron cavalry as vanguard, and linked themselves with hooked ropes so that even when dead they did not fall from the horse.
translations.idiomatic: They wore heavy armor on fine horses, led with iron cavalry linked by hooked ropes so that even in death they did not fall from the saddle.

sentences.zh: 其民俗勇悍，衣冠、騎乘、土產品物、子姓傳國，亦略知其大概耳。

translations.literal: Their people by custom were fierce and bold; in dress, mounts, local products, and succession of surnames and transmission of the state, one may know their general outline.
translations.idiomatic: Their folk were by nature fierce; their dress, horses, products, royal surnames, and succession may be known in broad outline.

sentences.zh: 初，西夏臣宋有年，賜姓曰趙；

translations.literal: At first, while Western Xia was subject to Song for years, they were granted the surname Zhao;
translations.idiomatic: At first, while long subject to Song, Xia received the surname Zhao;

sentences.zh: 迨遼聖宗統和四年，繼遷叛宋，始來附遼，授特進檢校太師、都督夏州諸軍事，遂復姓李。

translations.literal: When in the fourth year of Tonghe under Liao Emperor Shenzong, Jiqian rebelled against Song and first came to attach himself to Liao, he was appointed Special Advancement, Honorary Grand Preceptor, and Military Commissioner of Xia Prefecture and All Forces, and thus resumed the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tonghe, Jiqian defected from Song to Liao, was made Special Advancement and Honorary Grand Preceptor with command of Xia forces, and took back the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 十月，遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, envoys came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month they presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 六年，入貢。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year they offered tribute.

sentences.zh: 七年，來貢，以王子帳耶律襄之女封義成公主，下嫁繼遷。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, they came to pay tribute; the daughter of Yelü Xiang of the Imperial Son-in-law Account was enfeoffed as Princess Yicheng and given in marriage to Jiqian.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year they came with tribute; Yelü Xiang's daughter was made Princess Yicheng and married to Jiqian.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，來謝。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year, they came to express thanks.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year they came to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 三月，又來貢。

translations.literal: In the third month, they again came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month they presented tribute again.

sentences.zh: 九月，繼遷遣使獻宋俘。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Jiqian sent envoys presenting Song captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Jiqian sent envoys with captives taken from Song.

sentences.zh: 十月，以敗宋軍來告。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, they came to report having defeated the Song army.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month they reported a victory over Song.

sentences.zh: 十二月，下宋麟、鄜等州，來告，遣使封繼遷為夏國王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, having taken Song prefectures Lin and Fu and others, they came to report; envoys were sent to enfeoff Jiqian as King of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, after capturing Lin, Fu, and other Song prefectures, they reported the feat; envoys invested Jiqian as King of Xia.

sentences.zh: 九年二月，遣使告伐宋之捷。

translations.literal: In the second month of the ninth year, envoys came to report victory over Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the ninth year, envoys announced victory over Song.

sentences.zh: 四月，遣李知白來謝封冊。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Li Zhibai was sent to thank the court for the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, Li Zhibai came to thank the court for the investiture.

sentences.zh: 七月，復綏、銀二州，來告。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, they recovered Sui and Yin prefectures and came to report.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, after retaking Sui and Yin, they reported to the court.

sentences.zh: 十月，繼遷以宋所授敕命，遣使來上。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Jiqian sent the edicts and commissions conferred by Song; envoys came to present them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Jiqian sent up the patents Song had granted him.

sentences.zh: 是月，定難軍節度使李繼捧來附，授開府儀同三司、檢校太師，兼侍中，封西平王，仍賜推忠效順啟聖定難功臣。

translations.literal: In that month, Li Jibeng, Military Commissioner of Dingnan Army, came to attach himself; he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies, Honorary Grand Preceptor, and Concurrent Palace Attendant, enfeoffed as Western Peace Prince, and still granted the title of Meritous Minister Loyal and Obedient, Enlightening and Sagely, Stabilizing Dingnan.
translations.idiomatic: That month, Dingnan Military Commissioner Li Jibeng submitted; he was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Honorary Grand Preceptor, Palace Attendant, Western Peace Prince, with the merit title Loyal and Obedient, Enlightening and Sagely, Stabilizing Dingnan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，繼遷潛附於宋，遣韓德威持詔諭之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Jiqian secretly attached himself to Song; Han Dewei was sent with an edict to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Jiqian secretly leaned toward Song; Han Dewei was dispatched with an edict to admonish him.

sentences.zh: 十年二月，韓德威還，奏繼遷托故不出，至靈州俘掠以還。

translations.literal: In the second month of the tenth year, Han Dewei returned and reported that Jiqian made excuses and would not come out; he reached Ling Prefecture, seized captives, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the tenth year, Han Dewei returned reporting that Jiqian pleaded illness and would not appear; he raided Ling Prefecture and withdrew with captives.

sentences.zh: 西夏遣使來奏德威俘掠，賜詔撫諭。

translations.literal: Western Xia sent envoys to report Han Dewei's seizure of captives; an edict was bestowed to console and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Xia envoys complained of Han Dewei's raid; the court sent a comforting edict.

sentences.zh: 十月，來貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month they presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 十二年，入貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year they offered tribute.

sentences.zh: 十三年，敗宋師，遣使來告。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, they defeated the Song army and sent envoys to report.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, after defeating Song, they sent envoys with the news.

sentences.zh: 十四年，又來貢。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, they again came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year they came with tribute again.

sentences.zh: 十五年三月，以破宋兵來告，封繼遷為西平王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifteenth year, they came to report defeating Song troops; Jiqian was enfeoffed as Western Peace Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifteenth year, reporting victory over Song, Jiqian was enfeoffed Western Peace Prince.

sentences.zh: 六月，遣使來謝封冊。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, envoys came to thank the court for the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, envoys thanked the court for the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 十六年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year they presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 十八年，授繼遷子德明朔方軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Jiqian's son Deming was appointed Military Commissioner of Shuofang Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, Jiqian's son Deming was made Military Commissioner of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 十九年，遣李文冀來貢。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Li Wenyi was sent to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, Li Wenyi came with tribute.

sentences.zh: 六月，奏下宋恒、環、慶三州，賜詔褒美。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, they reported taking Song prefectures Heng, Huan, and Qing; an edict was bestowed praising them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, they reported capturing Heng, Huan, and Qing; the court issued a commendatory edict.

sentences.zh: 二十年，遣使來進馬、駝。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, envoys came presenting horses and camels.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, envoys brought horses and camels.

sentences.zh: 六月，遣劉仁勖來告下靈州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Liu Renxu was sent to report the capture of Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Liu Renxu reported the fall of Ling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，繼遷薨，其子德昭遣使來告。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, Jiqian died; his son Dezhao sent envoys to announce it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, Jiqian died; his son Dezhao reported the death.

sentences.zh: 六月，贈繼遷尚書令，遣西上閣門使丁振吊慰。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Jiqian was posthumously granted Minister of Works; Western Upper Gate Commissioner Ding Zhen was sent to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Jiqian was posthumously made Minister of Works and Ding Zhen was sent to mourn.

sentences.zh: 八月，德昭遣使來謝吊贈。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Dezhao sent envoys to thank the court for the mourning gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Dezhao sent envoys to thank the court for condolence gifts.

sentences.zh: 二十二年三月，德昭遣使上繼遷遺留物。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-second year, Dezhao sent envoys presenting objects left by Jiqian.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twenty-second year, Dezhao sent Jiqian's remaining possessions.

sentences.zh: 七月，封德昭為西平王。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Dezhao was enfeoffed as Western Peace Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Dezhao was enfeoffed Western Peace Prince.

sentences.zh: 十月，遣使來謝封冊。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, envoys came to thank the court for the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, envoys thanked the court for the investiture.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，下宋青城，來告。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, they took Song's Qingcheng and came to report.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, they reported capturing Song's Qingcheng.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，德昭母薨，遣使吊祭，起復。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Dezhao's mother died; envoys were sent to offer libations and sacrifices, and he was ordered to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, upon Dezhao's mother's death, envoys performed sacrifices and ordered his return from mourning.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，承天皇太后崩，遣使報哀於夏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, the Empress Dowager Chengtian died; envoys were sent to announce the mourning to Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, Empress Dowager Chengtian died; envoys announced the mourning to Xia.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，遣使冊德昭為夏國王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, envoys were sent to invest Dezhao as King of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, Dezhao was invested King of Xia.

sentences.zh: 開泰元年，德昭遣使進良馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaitai, Dezhao sent envoys presenting fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaitai, Dezhao sent fine horses.

sentences.zh: 二年，遣使引進使李延弘賜夏國王李德昭及義成公主車馬。

translations.literal: In the second year, Introducing Commissioner Li Yanhong was sent to bestow carriages and horses on King of Xia Li Dezhao and Princess Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Introducing Commissioner Li Yanhong granted carriages and horses to King Li Dezhao and Princess Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 太平元年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiping, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiping they presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 十一年，聖宗崩，報哀於夏，德昭遣使來進賻幣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Emperor Shenzong died; mourning was announced to Xia, and Dezhao sent envoys presenting funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, upon Shenzong's death, Xia was notified; Dezhao sent funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 興宗即位，以興平公主下嫁李元昊，以元昊為駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xingzong succeeded, Princess Xingping was given in marriage to Li Yuanhao, and Yuanhao was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: At Xingzong's accession, Princess Xingping married Li Yuanhao, who was made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 重熙元年，夏國遣使來賀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongxi, envoys from Xia came to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongxi, Xia envoys came to congratulate.

sentences.zh: 李德昭薨，冊其子夏國公元昊為王。

translations.literal: Li Dezhao died; his son, King of Xia Li Yuanhao, was invested as king.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dezhao died; his son Li Yuanhao was invested King of Xia.

sentences.zh: 二年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the second year, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year they offered tribute.

sentences.zh: 十二月，禁夏國使沿路私市金鐵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Xia envoys were forbidden to trade gold and iron privately along the route.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, private trade in gold and iron by Xia envoys along the road was banned.

sentences.zh: 七年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year they presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 李元昊與平公主不諧，公主薨，遣北院承旨耶律庶成持詔問之。

translations.literal: Li Yuanhao was not harmonious with Princess Ping; when the princess died, Northern Chancellery Attendant Yelü Shucheng was sent with an edict to inquire into the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanhao quarreled with Princess Ping; when she died, Northern Chancellery Attendant Yelü Shucheng was sent to investigate.

sentences.zh: 九年，宋遣郭禎以伐夏來報。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Song sent Guo Zhen to report that they were attacking Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, Song dispatched Guo Zhen to announce their campaign against Xia.

sentences.zh: 十年，夏國獻所俘宋將及生口。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Xia presented Song generals they had captured and living captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, Xia offered captured Song commanders and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遣使問宋興師伐夏之由。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, envoys were sent to ask Song the reason for raising troops to attack Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, envoys inquired of Song why it had mobilized against Xia.

sentences.zh: 十二月，禁吐渾鬻馬於夏，沿邊築障塞以防之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Tuyuhun were forbidden to sell horses to Xia, and barrier fortifications were built along the border to guard against it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Tuyuhun horse sales to Xia were banned and border barriers were erected.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，遣同知析津府事耶律敵烈、樞密都承旨王惟吉諭夏國與宋和。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year, Associate Commissioner of the Xijin Prefecture Yelü Dilie and Bureau of Military Affairs Chief Administrator Wang Weiji were sent to instruct Xia to make peace with Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year, Yelü Dilie and Wang Weiji were dispatched to urge Xia and Song to reconcile.

sentences.zh: 二月，元昊以加上尊號，遣使來賀。

translations.literal: In the second month, because of the addition of an honorific title, Yuanhao sent envoys to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Yuanhao sent envoys to congratulate the bestowal of an honorific title.

sentences.zh: 耶律敵烈等使夏國還，奏元昊罷兵，遣使報宋。

translations.literal: Yelü Dilie and others returned from their mission to Xia and reported that Yuanhao had ceased hostilities and sent envoys to notify Song.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Dilie and his party returned from Xia reporting that Yuanhao had halted fighting and notified Song.

sentences.zh: 四月，夏國遣使進馬、駝。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Xia sent envoys presenting horses and camels.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, Xia envoys brought horses and camels.

sentences.zh: 七月，元昊上表請伐宋，不從。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Yuanhao submitted a memorial requesting permission to attack Song; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Yuanhao petitioned to attack Song; the request was refused.

sentences.zh: 十月，夏人侵党項，遣延昌宮使高家奴讓之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Xia people invaded the Dangxiang; Palace Commissioner of the Yanchang Palace Gao Jianu was sent to reprove them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Xia raided the Dangxiang; Gao Jianu of the Yanchang Palace was sent to rebuke them.

sentences.zh: 十三年四月，党項及山西部族節度使屈烈以五部叛入西夏，詔征諸道兵討之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year, the Dangxiang and Qu Lie, Military Commissioner of the Western Mountain Tribes, with five tribes rebelled and entered Western Xia; an edict ordered troops of all circuits to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year, the Dangxiang and Western Mountain Commissioner Qu Lie led five tribes into Xia; troops from all circuits were ordered to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 六月，阻卜酋長烏八遣其子執元昊所遣求援使窊邑改來。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Zubu chieftain Wuba sent his son with the Xia envoy for aid, Woyigai, whom he had seized.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Zubu chief Wuba sent his son with the captured Xia relief envoy Woyigai.

sentences.zh: 八月，夏使對不以情，羈之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Xia envoy answered without sincerity and was detained.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, a Xia envoy answered insincerely and was held.

sentences.zh: 使復來，詢事宜不實對，笞之。

translations.literal: When the envoy came again and was questioned on affairs but answered untruthfully, he was flogged.
translations.idiomatic: When another envoy came and gave false answers, he was beaten.

sentences.zh: 十月，元昊上表謝罪，欲收集叛黨以獻，從之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Yuanhao submitted a memorial begging forgiveness and wishing to gather the rebel tribes to present them; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Yuanhao apologized and offered to round up the rebels; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 進方物，命北院樞密副使蕭革迓之。

translations.literal: He presented local products; Northern Chancellery Vice Commissioner Xiao Ge was ordered to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent tribute; Vice Commissioner Xiao Ge of the Northern Chancellery received him.

sentences.zh: 元昊親率党項三部來降，詰其納叛背盟，元昊伏罪。

translations.literal: Yuanhao personally led three Dangxiang tribes to surrender; he was charged with accepting rebels and breaking the alliance, and Yuanhao confessed his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao led three Dangxiang tribes to submit; rebuked for harboring rebels and breaking treaty, he confessed.

sentences.zh: 初，夏人執蕭胡睹，至是，請以被執者來歸。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Xia had seized Xiao Huzhao; now they asked to return those who had been seized.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia had earlier captured Xiao Huzhao; now they offered to exchange prisoners.

sentences.zh: 詔所留夏使亦還其國。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that the Xia envoys detained here also be returned to their state.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered detained Xia envoys returned home.

sentences.zh: 十二月，胡睹來歸，又遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Huzhao returned, and envoys again came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Huzhao came back and Xia again sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 十七年，元昊薨，其子諒祚遣使來告，上其父遺留物。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Yuanhao died; his son Liangzuo sent envoys to announce it and presented objects left by his father.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, Yuanhao died; his son Liangzuo reported the death and sent his father's remaining goods.

sentences.zh: 鐵不得國乞以本部軍助攻夏國，不許。

translations.literal: Tiedebude State begged to use its tribal army to assist in attacking Xia; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiedebude tribe asked to join the attack on Xia; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 十八年，復議伐夏，留其賀正使不遣，遣北院樞密副使蕭惟信以伐夏告宋。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, an attack on Xia was again discussed; their New Year congratulatory envoys were detained, and Northern Chancellery Vice Commissioner Xiao Weixin was sent to inform Song of the campaign against Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, war on Xia was reconsidered; Xia New Year envoys were held and Xiao Weixin notified Song of the expedition.

sentences.zh: 六月，夏國遣使來貢，留之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Xia sent envoys to pay tribute; they were detained.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Xia tribute envoys were detained.

sentences.zh: 七月，親征。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the emperor campaigned in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, the emperor led the campaign personally.

sentences.zh: 八月，渡河，夏人遁。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, they crossed the river; the Xia fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, after crossing the river, the Xia withdrew.

sentences.zh: 九月，蕭惠為夏人所敗。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Xiao Hui was defeated by the Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Xiao Hui was routed by Xia forces.

sentences.zh: 十月，招討使耶律敵古率阻卜軍至賀蘭山，獲元昊妻及其官屬。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Pacification Commissioner Yelü Digu led Zubu troops to Helan Mountain and captured Yuanhao's wife and his officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Yelü Digu led Zubu troops to Helan Mountain and seized Yuanhao's wife and officials.

sentences.zh: 遇其軍三千來拒，殪之；

translations.literal: They met their army of three thousand coming to resist and destroyed it;
translations.idiomatic: They met three thousand Xia troops, annihilated them;

sentences.zh: 詳穩蕭慈氏奴、南克耶律斡裏歿於陣。

translations.literal: Detailed commander Xiao Cishinu and Nankoye Yelü Wolie perished in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Detailed commander Xiao Cishinu and Yelü Wolie of Nankoye fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 十九年正月，遣使問罪於夏。

translations.literal: In the first month of the nineteenth year, envoys were sent to demand satisfaction from Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the nineteenth year, envoys were sent to press charges against Xia.

sentences.zh: 夏將窪普等攻金肅城，耶律高家奴等破之，窪普被創遁去，殺猥貨乙靈紀。

translations.literal: Xia generals Wapu and others attacked Jinsu City; Yelü Gao Jianu and others defeated them; Wapu was wounded and fled, and Weihuo Yilingji was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Xia general Wapu attacked Jinsu; Yelü Gao Jianu routed him; Wapu fled wounded and Weihuo Yilingji was slain.

sentences.zh: 三月，殿前都點檢蕭叠裏得與夏軍戰於三角川，敗之。

translations.literal: In the third month, Chief Palace Inspector Xiao Dielide fought the Xia army at Sanjiao River and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Xiao Dielide defeated the Xia at Sanjiao River.

sentences.zh: 招討使蕭蒲奴、北院大王宜新等帥師伐夏，都部署別古得為監戰。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Xiao Punu, Northern Chancellery King Yixin, and others led troops against Xia; Chief Deployer Biegude was battle overseer.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Punu, King Yixin of the Northern Chancellery, and others invaded Xia with Biegude as overseer.

sentences.zh: 五月，蕭蒲奴等入夏境，不遇敵，縱軍俘掠而還。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Xiao Punu and others entered Xia territory, met no enemy, and let the army seize captives and return.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Xiao Punu entered Xia, found no foe, and withdrew after plundering.

sentences.zh: 夏國窪普來降。

translations.literal: Wapu of Xia came over to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xia's Wapu surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十月，李諒祚母遣使乞依舊稱臣。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Liangzuo's mother sent envoys begging to submit as a subject as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Liangzuo's mother asked to resume vassal status.

sentences.zh: 十二月，諒祚上表如母訓。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Liangzuo submitted a memorial as his mother had instructed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Liangzuo memorialized as his mother directed.

sentences.zh: 二十年二月，遣使索党項叛戶。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twentieth year, envoys were sent to demand the rebel Dangxiang households.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twentieth year, envoys demanded the rebel Dangxiang clans.

sentences.zh: 五月，蕭爻括使夏回，進諒祚母表，乞代党項權進馬駝牛羊等物；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Xiao Yaogua returned from Xia and presented Liangzuo's mother's memorial, begging to present horses, camels, cattle, and sheep on behalf of the Dangxiang;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Xiao Yaogua returned with Liangzuo's mother's petition to offer horses, camels, cattle, and sheep for the Dangxiang;

sentences.zh: 又求唐隆鎮，仍乞罷所建城邑。

translations.literal: she also requested Tanglong Garrison and further begged that the fortified towns that had been built be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: she also sought Tanglong Garrison and asked that border towns be dismantled.

sentences.zh: 以詔答之。

translations.literal: An edict was sent in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The court answered by edict.

sentences.zh: 六月，獲元昊妻，及俘到夏人置於蘇州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Yuanhao's wife was captured, and Xia prisoners taken were placed in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Yuanhao's wife was taken and Xia captives held at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十一年十月，諒祚遣使乞弛邊備，遣爻括賫詔諭之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twenty-first year, Liangzuo sent envoys begging that border defenses be relaxed; Yaogua was sent bearing an edict to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the twenty-first year, Liangzuo asked to ease border garrisons; Yaogua bore an edict in reply.

sentences.zh: 二十二年七月，諒祚進降表，遣林牙高家奴賫詔撫諭。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-second year, Liangzuo submitted a surrender memorial; Palace Secretary Gao Jianu was sent bearing an edict to console and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-second year, Liangzuo submitted surrender; Gao Jianu was sent with a comforting edict.

sentences.zh: 二十三年正月，貢方物。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-third year, local products were presented as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-third year, they presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 五月，乞進馬駝，詔歲貢之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, they begged to present horses and camels; an edict ordered annual tribute of them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, they asked to offer horses and camels; annual tribute was decreed.

sentences.zh: 七月，諒祚遣使求婚。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Liangzuo sent envoys requesting a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Liangzuo sought a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 十月，進誓表。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, an oath memorial was presented.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, he submitted an oath memorial.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，興宗崩，遣使報哀於夏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Emperor Xingzong died; envoys were sent to announce the mourning to Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, upon Xingzong's death, Xia was notified.

sentences.zh: 道宗即位，清寧元年，遣使來賀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daozong succeeded, in the first year of Qingning envoys came to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: At Daozong's accession, in the first year of Qingning, Xia envoys came to congratulate.

sentences.zh: 九月，以先帝遺物賜夏。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, objects left by the late emperor were bestowed on Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the late emperor's gifts were granted to Xia.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，遣使會葬。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year, envoys were sent to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year, envoys came for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，禁民鬻銅於夏。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year, the people were forbidden to sell copper to Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year, private copper sales to Xia were banned.

sentences.zh: 咸雍元年五月，來貢。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Xianyong, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Xianyong they presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 三年十一月，遣使進回鶻僧、金佛、《梵覺經》。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year, envoys were sent presenting Uyghur monks, a gold Buddha, and the 《Fanjue Sutra》.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year, they sent Uyghur monks, a gold Buddha, and the 《Fanjue Sutra》.

sentences.zh: 十二月，諒祚薨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Liangzuo died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Liangzuo died.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，諒祚子秉常遣使報哀，即遣使吊祭。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, Liangzuo's son Bingchang sent envoys to announce the mourning, and envoys were immediately sent to offer libations and sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year, Bingchang reported his father's death; envoys were sent at once to mourn.

sentences.zh: 秉常上其父遺物。

translations.literal: Bingchang presented his father's remaining objects.
translations.idiomatic: Bingchang sent his father's remaining possessions.

sentences.zh: 十月，冊秉常為夏國王。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Bingchang was invested as King of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Bingchang was invested King of Xia.

sentences.zh: 十二月，來貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month they offered tribute.

sentences.zh: 五年七月，遣使來謝封冊，閏十一月，秉常乞賜印綬。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year, envoys came to thank the court for the investiture; in the intercalary eleventh month, Bingchang begged that seals and cords be bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year, envoys thanked the court for investiture; in the intercalary eleventh month, Bingchang asked for seals and cords.

sentences.zh: 九年，遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, envoys came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, tribute envoys arrived.

sentences.zh: 大康二年正月，仁懿皇后崩，遣使報哀於夏，以皇太后遺物賜之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Dakang, Empress Renyi died; envoys were sent to announce the mourning to Xia, and objects left by the Empress Dowager were bestowed on them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Dakang, upon Empress Renyi's death, Xia was notified and given the Empress Dowager's gifts.

sentences.zh: 遣使來吊祭。

translations.literal: Envoys came to offer libations and sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys came to perform mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 五年，來貢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, they came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year they presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 八年二月，遣使以所獲宋將張天益來獻。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year, envoys were sent presenting the Song general Zhang Tianyi whom they had captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year, they offered the captured Song general Zhang Tianyi.

sentences.zh: 大安元年十月，秉常遣使報其母哀。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Da'an, Bingchang sent envoys to announce his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Da'an, Bingchang reported his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 二年十月，秉常薨，遣使詔其子乾順知國事。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year, Bingchang died; envoys were sent with an edict ordering his son Qianshun to manage state affairs provisionally.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year, Bingchang died; an edict put his son Qianshun in provisional charge.

sentences.zh: 十二月，李乾順遣使上其父秉常遺物。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Li Qianshun sent envoys presenting his father Bingchang's remaining objects.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Qianshun sent his father's remaining goods.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，冊乾順為夏國王。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year, Qianshun was invested as King of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year, Qianshun was invested King of Xia.

sentences.zh: 五年六月，遣使來謝封冊。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year, envoys came to thank the court for the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year, envoys thanked the court for investiture.

sentences.zh: 八年六月，夏為宋所侵，遣使乞援。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eighth year, Xia was invaded by Song and sent envoys begging for aid.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the eighth year, invaded by Song, Xia asked for help.

sentences.zh: 壽隆三年六月，以宋人置壁壘於要地，遣使來告。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Shoulong, because Song had placed fortifications at strategic points, envoys came to report it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year of Shoulong, Xia reported Song fortifications at key points.

sentences.zh: 四年六月，求援。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year, they begged for aid.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year, they requested aid.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遣樞密直學士耶律儼使宋，諷與夏和。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Bureau of Military Affairs Direct Academician Yelü Yan was sent to Song to hint that they should make peace with Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Yelü Yan was sent to Song to urge reconciliation with Xia.

sentences.zh: 夏復遣使來求援。

translations.literal: Xia again sent envoys begging for aid.
translations.idiomatic: Xia again asked for military aid.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，詔乾順伐拔思母等部。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, an edict ordered Qianshun to attack the Basimu and other tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year, Qianshun was ordered to campaign against the Basimu tribes.

sentences.zh: 十一月，夏以宋人罷兵，遣使來謝。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, because Song had ceased hostilities, Xia sent envoys to express thanks.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, with Song's withdrawal, Xia sent thanks.

sentences.zh: 六年十一月，遣使請尚公主。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the sixth year, envoys were sent requesting marriage to an imperial princess.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the sixth year, envoys sought an imperial princess in marriage.

sentences.zh: 七年，道宗崩，遣使告哀於夏。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Emperor Daozong died; envoys were sent to announce the mourning to Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, upon Daozong's death, Xia was notified.

sentences.zh: 遣使來慰奠。

translations.literal: Envoys came to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys came to console the court.

sentences.zh: 論曰：高麗、西夏之事遼，雖嘗請婚下嫁，烏足以得其固誌哉？

translations.literal: Discussion: The affairs of Goryeo and Western Xia with Liao—although they sometimes requested marriage and received brides down—how could that secure their steadfast intent?
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Though Goryeo and Western Xia sometimes sought Liao brides, marriage alone could not bind their true loyalties?

sentences.zh: 三韓接壤，反覆易知；

translations.literal: The Three Han bordered Liao directly, and their shifts back and forth were easy to discern;
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo lay adjacent to Liao, its reversals plain to see;

sentences.zh: 涼州負遠，納叛侵疆。

translations.literal: Liangzhou lay far away, and they harbored rebels and encroached on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Xia held distant Liangzhou, sheltering defectors and raiding the border.

sentences.zh: 乘隙輒動，貢使方往，事釁隨生。

translations.literal: Seizing every opening they stirred; tribute envoys had barely set out when incidents arose.
translations.idiomatic: They struck at every chance; no sooner had tribute envoys departed than trouble broke out.

sentences.zh: 興師問罪，屢煩親征，取勝固多，敗亦貽悔。

translations.literal: Raising armies to demand satisfaction, the emperors repeatedly campaigned in person; victories were many, yet defeats also brought regret.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns to punish them drew the emperors repeatedly to the field; wins were frequent, but defeats left lasting regret.

sentences.zh: 昔吳趙咨對魏之言曰：「大國有征伐之兵，小國有備禦之固。

translations.literal: In former times Wu's Zhao Zi said to Wei: "Great states have armies for campaigning; small states have defenses that are firm."
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Zhao Zi of Wu told Wei: "Great powers wage war; small states hold fast in defense."

sentences.zh: 」豈其然乎！

translations.literal: Is it really so!
translations.idiomatic: Was he not right!

sentences.zh: 先王柔遠，以德而不以力，尚矣。

translations.literal: The former kings soothed the distant by virtue and not by force—how lofty that was.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings won the far frontier through virtue, not force—how exalted a policy.

sentences.zh: 遼亡，求援二國，雖能出師，豈金敵哉！

translations.literal: When Liao perished, they begged aid from the two states; though troops could be sent forth, how could they match the Jin enemy!
translations.idiomatic: At Liao's fall they sought help from Goryeo and Xia; armies could march, but none could stand against the Jin!
